audited_source_files.description: CADD explainable rule engine and candidate scoring implementation (v2.0.0-phase2)
CESO telemetry aggregation service mapping raw metrics to NetworkState
Benchmark runner orchestrating testbed scenarios across experimental arms

ARM_3_RULE_BASED.preprocessing_and_rules: Evaluates discrete boolean conditions (e.g., packet_loss_pct > 15.0, rtt_ms > 100.0, is_up == False). Matches exact rule patterns to trigger DiagnosticEvidence outputs.
ARM_3_RULE_BASED.confidence_logic: Fixed binary or threshold confidence without continuous margin discounting.
ARM_3_RULE_BASED.prediction_mapping: Returns standard diagnosis labels (e.g. LINK_FLAPPING, ROUTE_LEAK, HARDWARE_FAULT) matching evaluation target schema.

ARM_4_PHASE2_BASELINE.preprocessing_and_rules: Computes continuous multi-attribute candidate score S(c) in [0, 1]. Applies deterministic tie-breaking priority list and heuristic margin confidence formula: C = round(S(c*)(1 - 0.5 * S(c^(2))), 4).
ARM_4_PHASE2_BASELINE.confidence_logic: Margin discounting based on second-highest candidate score. Escalates if confidence falls below baseline threshold.
ARM_4_PHASE2_BASELINE.prediction_mapping: Maps candidate c* to standard evaluation diagnosis category.
ARM_4_PHASE2_BASELINE.determinism: Fully deterministic for pre-extracted static NetworkState.

ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.algorithm_name: Live CESO Telemetry Aggregation + CADE Candidate Scoring
ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.preprocessing_and_rules: Dynamically aggregates multi-node live telemetry via CESOService into NetworkState, then executes CADE continuous candidate scoring S(c) and margin confidence discounting.
ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.confidence_logic: Margin-discounted continuous confidence computed from live aggregated telemetry state.
ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.prediction_mapping: Outputs diagnosis category mapped to evaluation target schema.
ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.determinism: Deterministic relative to recorded live telemetry snapshot.

ARM_3_vs_ARM_4.rationale: Arm 3 uses discrete boolean rule matching without continuous multi-attribute scoring or margin confidence discounting, whereas Arm 4 evaluates continuous candidate scores S(c) with second-highest score margin confidence calculation.

ARM_3_vs_ARM_5.rationale: Arm 3 processes static state with discrete rule matching, while Arm 5 combines dynamic multi-node live telemetry aggregation (CESO) with continuous candidate scoring (CADE).

ARM_4_vs_ARM_5.rationale: Arm 4 evaluates static pre-extracted telemetry state snapshots, whereas Arm 5 integrates live end-to-end multi-metric telemetry extraction through CESOService prior to CADE scoring.

ARM_3_RULE_BASED.evidence: backend/app/cadd/engine.py (lines 161-230). Evaluates only telemetry fields (packet_loss_pct, rtt_ms, is_up); no access to expected fault labels or scenario metadata.

ARM_4_PHASE2_BASELINE.data_flow_path: NetworkState -> Candidate Score S(c) -> Margin Discount -> Diagnostic output
ARM_4_PHASE2_BASELINE.evidence: backend/app/cadd/engine.py (lines 231-380). Inputs only operational metrics; ground-truth labels are strictly isolated in benchmark evaluation code.

ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.data_flow_path: Live Telemetry -> CESOService -> NetworkState -> CADE Engine -> Diagnostic output
ARM_5_CESO_CADE_NO_LLM.evidence: backend/app/ceso/service.py (lines 45-180). Telemetry collection queries raw interfaces/metrics without access to evaluation labels.

fairness_and_metric_support.input_equivalence: PASS — All arms receive identical network telemetry streams or state representations corresponding to the exact same observation window.
fairness_and_metric_support.seed_control: PASS — Paired execution seeds and fixed fault injection schedules ensure identical scenario progression across arms.

material_issues.description: Live telemetry extraction in ARM_5 introduces slight measurement overhead relative to pre-extracted static state in ARM_4, which must be tracked as instrumentation latency.
material_issues.recommended_correction: Measure raw CADE compute time separately from CESO data collection latency in evaluation metrics.
